5.0.s.en: (1) Life in eternity and preparing for it

5.0.1.en: Paul says that every believer knows with certainty and faith that if he dies or is martyred as a result of the afflictions, sufferings or hardships around him, he has in heaven an eternal, abiding life. He likens the body to an earthly tent that can be taken down at any time, but when it is taken down it transfers us to a great heavenly building not made with hands, and God will clothe us with a body of light, by which is meant the body of the resurrection.

5.1.0.en: This: the tent, that is, the body.

5.1.1.en: We groan: we ache from the sufferings and persecutions that pass over us in life.

5.1.2.en: Clothed upon: our fleshly bodies are changed into bodies of light.

5.1.3.en: Our house which is from heaven: our bodies of light, with which we will live in the Kingdom.

5.1.4.en: When Paul suffers during his life on earth, his heart is lifted to heaven, and he longs for the body of light that he will receive, which is not exposed to pain and lasts forever. Perhaps Paul, in the intensity of his longing for heaven, wished that Christ would come in His Second Coming during Paul's life on earth, and then he would not die and have his body placed in the tomb, but the material body would be changed and he would be clothed upon with a body of light, that is, the material body would be changed and disappear and become a body of light suited to being in heaven, as he mentioned this matter in (1 Cor 15:51, 52).

5.2.1.en: Naked: the spirit without a body.

5.2.2.en: The Apostle continues his talk about his longing for the Second Coming and the change of the earthly body into a body of light, saying that he will be clothed with this new body and his spirit will not be found naked without a body. That is, man will live in heaven with his spirit and his body, but with a new body of light that befits life in heaven.

5.3.0.en: St. Paul affirms that the labors of the body make him long, not for death and for placing his body in the tomb, but for the swift coming of Christ, so that his body is changed into a body of light. He likens the body of light to a garment that covers the earthly body and swallows it up. Thus the earthly is changed into the luminous.

5.4.1.en: For the selfsame thing: to live in the Kingdom.

5.4.2.en: The earnest of the Spirit: a taste of a spiritual relationship with God on earth.

5.4.3.en: Paul shows that God's purpose in creating us is that we live with Him in heaven, and that our earthly life is temporary. Therefore He gives us, by the Holy Spirit, the pledge of the Kingdom of Heaven while we are on earth; that is, He gives us the enjoyment of a relationship with God through spiritual practices and the Sacraments of the Church, so that we may be able to bear the labors of earth and at the same time our longings toward heaven increase.

5.5.0.en: At home in the body: attached to the desires of the body.

5.5.1.en: The Apostle affirms a firm truth, which is that if we are occupied with bodily desires, we shall become strangers to God, far from the spiritual life.

5.6.0.en: The believing children of God see God by faith, so they are not occupied with the evil desires of the body that they see with their eyes, because they fear God and love Him and prepare for eternity.

5.7.0.en: The natural condition of the children of God is to keep away from evil desires so as to become true children of God, that is, citizens fit for the life of heaven.

5.8.0.en: The purpose and goal of man's life is to please God, whether he is in the body on earth or has left the body and been lifted up to heaven. Those on earth and those in heaven have the same goal, which is to please God.

5.9.0.en: We must appear before the judgment seat of Christ: the Last Judgment.

5.9.1.en: The things done in his body: man's works on earth.

5.9.2.en: In sum, we must not forget that we shall stand before God on the Day of Judgment and be held to account for all our words, works and thoughts, and we shall be rewarded with the Kingdom if we have done good, or punished with eternal torment if we have done evil.

5.9.3.en: Do you think of heaven and feel that your earthly life is only a brief period and that we must go from the land of exile to Paradise? Do you long for God and feel the weight of the material things that deprive you of God and of fellowship with Him?

5.9.4.en: Therefore strive with all your strength to have on this earth fellowship with God and pleasing works and a constant love for His Kingdom, so that you may enjoy constant fellowship with Him in heaven, and reach that place from which sorrow, gloom and sighing have fled away.

5.10.s.en: (2) Paul's defense of himself before the false teachers

5.10.0.en: The terror of the Lord: that is, remembering always the Day of Judgment, so that we leave sin and live for righteousness.

5.10.1.en: We persuade men: preaching Christ the Savior and preparing for eternity.

5.10.2.en: As Paul remembers the Last Judgment, the fear of God arises in him, and he preaches and teaches accordingly so that all may prepare for eternity. And as he fears God, he feels that God sees all that is within him, of estrangement from evil desires and longing for the spiritual life. He wishes that the believers in Corinth would know and understand this by their living conscience, that is, the voice of God in them, meaning that they would trust Paul that he fears God and cares for his eternity.

5.11.0.en: In appearance: outward boasting, not real.

5.11.1.en: St. Paul did not intend, in defending himself, to praise himself, but wanted to establish his apostleship in order to confirm his teachings, and when the believers in Corinth see his strong relationship with God, they answer the false teachers, who cast doubt on his teachings and boast of outward matters in order to turn the believers away from the sound faith that Paul proclaims.

5.12.0.en: The false teachers accused Paul of mental derangement, and perhaps the greatest reason was his concern for preaching to the Gentiles, at which the Jews were enraged and accused him of derangement. He accepts being accused of derangement for the sake of serving God, but he warns the believers in Corinth that he is sane in every teaching with which he preached to them, and that there is no delirium or derangement in his teachings to them about Christ.

5.12.1.en: Defend yourself for the sake of God's glory and His service, not to glorify yourself and your honor. Seek the glory of God and not your own glory, and endure sufferings for His sake, and He will glorify you in the eyes of people, even if after a while, and then in the Kingdom of Heaven.

5.13.s.en: (3) Reconciling people with God so that they live for His love

5.13.0.en: The love of Christ constraineth us: it overwhelms us and urges us to love Him.

5.13.3.en: Christ died for us, so that instead of all of us dying, He died in our place. By His death our death was accomplished, and by His resurrection we all rise. How great is His love for us, for He bought us with His blood so that we may live for Him all our days.

5.14.0.en: St. Paul affirms here that Christ's death for us not only moves us to die to sin by leaving it, but we feel that we belong to Him, because He bought us with His blood, so we rise with Him to live for Him and to live in righteousness.

5.15.0.en: We know no man after the flesh: that is, as being a Jew or a Gentile, poor or rich, a man or a woman.....

5.15.1.en: Christ after the flesh: Christ as a man living as a Jewish man.

5.15.2.en: Yet now henceforth know we him no more: after faith we see Christ the God and Savior.

5.15.3.en: Since Christ bought us who believe in Him and we have become righteous in Him, we do not look at other believers according to their human circumstances, their race, and their social and financial standing, but we look at them as children of God and members of the Church. And also Christ, we see Him as God the Savior, the head of the Church, and not merely a good Jewish man who lived for a period of time on earth.

5.16.0.en: If we believe in Christ we receive the Sacrament of Baptism, in which we are born anew, and obtain a new nature, that is, we become a new creation that inclines to righteousness and keeps away from sin. Thus old things pass away from us, that is, sins and the passing concerns of the world, and we incline to imitate God and please Him, and all our senses and abilities become pure, seeking life with God.

5.17.0.en: All things: the believers in Christ who have received the new nature.

5.17.1.en: The ministry of reconciliation or the word of reconciliation: preaching reconciliation between God and man, that is, preaching Christianity.

5.17.2.en: The renewal of all believers is a grace from God, who removed the enmity and the barrier between us and Him, which is sin, by the death of Christ for us. By this we were reconciled with God, because the cause of the quarrel and separation, which is sin, has been removed, and this is what we receive in the Sacraments of Baptism, confession and Communion. His love for mankind increased in that He gave some of His children to proclaim and preach to others reconciliation with God, and this is the ministry carried out by the Apostles, the priests and the servants in every generation.

5.17.3.en: From the spirituality of the rite of the Divine Liturgy, the Church ordained that the first prayer in the Liturgy of the Faithful is the Prayer of Reconciliation, to declare to us and remind us of the reconciliation that Christ accomplished by the sacrifice of His body, so that we may remain in this reconciliation by Communion on the one hand and by a life of repentance and holiness on the other.

5.18.0.en: The Apostles and servants, in their preaching of Christ, are ambassadors for God, when they exhort people and call them to believe in Him and accept reconciliation with Him. This does not happen only when proclaiming to unbelievers, but also to believers, by their accepting reconciliation when they sin and being reconciled in the Sacrament of repentance and confession, and then partaking of the Holy Mysteries, so that they are united with God.

5.18.1.en: How great is the humility of God, who seeks reconciliation with His creation that is disobedient and rejects Him.

5.18.2.en: May you seek with love to be reconciled with the one who wrongs you, and rather with the one whom you have wronged, so that you may win everyone, even if you endure some reproach or rebuke from the other. And be confident that strength is love, forgiveness and the pursuit of reconciliation, so you will receive God's blessing and the love of others and live in peace.

5.19.0.en: God declares His inexpressible love in His Son Jesus Christ, the holy and righteous, as He said of Himself to the multitudes, "Which of you convinceth me of sin?" (Jn 8:46), in that He made Him, by His bearing our sins on the cross, stained with sin because of His love for us. Whoever looks at Him as He is crucified sees Him tortured and dying as a sinner, despite His perfect righteousness. And by Christ's death for us, we have become righteous and pure from sin through the Sacrament of Baptism, and whoever sees us sees the righteousness of God in us through our pure nature that comes out of the baptismal font. Paul's sincerity and forbearance toward the Corinthians

6.0.s.en: (1) Paul's sincerity and labor in the ministry

6.0.0.en: Paul, with the rest of the Apostles and servants, received the grace of working together with God to preach in His name, and this is the greatest honor a person can receive. Since his aim is to preach the grace of Christ that renews man through the Holy Sacraments, he asks the Corinthians not to receive this grace in vain, that is, to turn back from their sins and not be slothful in works of righteousness and goodness.

6.1.0.en: Paul urges the Corinthians to accept the faith without delay or hesitation, and he draws on the words of Isaiah in (Isa 49:8) to affirm to them the importance of seizing the opportunity by accepting the faith and thereby enjoying the work of God's grace in them.

6.2.0.en: In Paul's preaching of Christ, he was careful that no one should find fault with him, be offended because of him, and reject the faith. So he offered his love to all, endured many labors, and was careful in his conduct so that his ministry would be pure and draw as many as possible to Christ, such as his readiness not to eat meat if this could cause one of the weak believers to stumble (1 Cor 8:13).

6.3.0.en: St. Paul and his companions present the proof of their sincerity in the ministry and their love, that they may win all souls, and this proof is patience in enduring sufferings. He presents nine of them here, the first three of which any Christian may be exposed to, namely:

6.3.1.en: Distresses: sufferings that are hard to bear.

6.3.2.en: Necessities: deprivation of the things necessary for life, such as food or drink.

6.3.3.en: Afflictions: sufferings that hem a person in, so that he cannot escape from them.

6.3.4.en: Then he speaks of three sufferings to which he himself was exposed, namely:

6.3.5.en: Stripes: Paul was beaten eight times, five by the Jews and three by the Romans (ch. 11:

6.3.6.en: 24, 25). In imprisonments: Paul was thrown into prison many times, as at Philippi (Acts 16:23), Jerusalem (Acts 22:24) and Rome (Acts 28:16). Tumults: Paul was exposed to the agitation of crowds against him, and even attempts to kill him many times, as at Antioch of Pisidia (Acts 13:50), Lystra (Acts 14:19) and Jerusalem (Acts 21:30). Finally he speaks of three voluntary sufferings which the spiritually striving person takes upon himself, namely: Labors: this includes all the labors of spiritual striving and service.

6.3.7.en: Watchings: this means keeping vigil in prayer and service and enduring various sufferings.

6.3.8.en: Fastings: so that God may intervene in the life of the one who strives spiritually and in his service, whether they are communal fasts of the whole Church or individual fasts that the striving person adds to the general fasts.

6.4.0.en: St. Paul continues to declare his sincerity in the ministry, not only by enduring sufferings but also through virtues, and he tells us of nine of them, namely:

6.4.1.en: By pureness: that is, purity of heart and conduct.

6.4.2.en: By knowledge: knowledge of God and His work in the Church and the eternal Kingdom.

6.4.3.en: By longsuffering: when a person is filled with spiritual knowledge, he is longsuffering toward others and endures sufferings for God's sake.

6.4.4.en: By kindness: likewise he shows his love and tenderness toward others.

6.4.5.en: By the Holy Ghost: He supports the servant with many gifts and virtues.

6.4.6.en: By love unfeigned: the love offered to others becomes pure, without any ulterior purpose.

6.4.7.en: By the word of truth: the truth is God, so we proclaim Him in all our speech with others.

6.4.8.en: By the power of God: which supports the servants and the believers.

6.4.9.en: By the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left: works of righteousness are strong like armor on the right hand, that is, the various virtues, or on the left, that is, cutting off evil and sins.

6.5.0.en: Finally St. Paul shows the steadfastness of his love for God in all circumstances, in nine situations, namely:

6.5.1.en: By honour and dishonour: he continues in his love and service whether he receives honor from people or they insult and despise him.

6.5.2.en: By evil report and good report: a good reputation, the testimony of people and their praise of him, or on the contrary their condemnation and contempt of him and the spreading of slander against him.

6.5.3.en: As deceivers, and yet true: the Apostles and servants bear being accused of error and false teachings although their words are the truth and honesty that ought to be followed, because it is the right faith.

6.5.4.en: As unknown, and yet well known: people may neglect us and consider us fools, and we lose every position and standing among people. But we are confident that we are known to God and among the believers in the Church, who care to hear the word of God.

6.5.5.en: As dying, and behold, we live: the Apostles are often exposed to death, but God rescues them so that they live and continue their preaching.

6.5.6.en: As chastened, and not killed: they endure many sufferings as though they were chastisement for their sins, although they are a loving fellowship in the cross of Christ, but God rescues them from death and heals them of their wounds.

6.5.7.en: As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing: from the multitude of sufferings, sorrow appears on the Apostles, but in truth they are in inward peace and joy in the work of God, who rescues them and makes them feel His presence with them and gives them to enjoy inexpressible comforts.

6.5.8.en: As poor, yet making many rich: for the sake of Christ the Apostles appear in need and poverty in material things although they are rich in what is more important, which is the spiritual blessings that they pour out on others from God. As having nothing, and yet possessing all things: the Apostles appear as though they own nothing in the world and need everything, although they possess everything, that is, Christ, who satisfies them.

6.5.9.en: Do not be troubled if afflictions come upon you or people neglect you or you are exposed to various abuses, for all these are external. Only hold fast to God and seek Him with persistence, and you will experience Him and feel His presence with you and your heart will rejoice, so that you are not shaken by any suffering.

6.6.s.en: (2) Paul's love and forbearance toward the Corinthians

6.6.0.en: Our mouth is open: continuing to exhort and teach them.

6.6.1.en: Our heart is enlarged: filled with love, forgiveness and fatherhood.

6.6.2.en: Paul was not affected by the wrongs some of the Corinthians did to him when they followed false teachers and troubled him, but he continued to exhort them and love them, forgiving all their faults.

6.7.0.en: Ye are not straitened in us: that is, our hearts are open in love to you and have not been constrained by your wrongs. Straitened in your own bowels: you have created a constraint within yourselves by your siding against us, your following false teachers and your wronging us.

6.7.1.en: The Apostle declares his love for the Corinthians and assures them that he was not affected by the evil that is in their hearts toward him.

6.8.0.en: Now for a recompense in the same: as a result of my love toward you.

6.8.1.en: As unto my children: because he loves them as a father, since he begot them as children of Christ by his preaching among them.

6.8.2.en: Paul calls the Corinthians to abandon the evil in their hearts toward him, and to love him as he loves them, because he is their father and seeks their salvation.

6.8.3.en: When others wrong you, have pity on them, because sin is weakness. In this way the evil within them becomes limited until you put an end to it by your prayers and your love. That is, keep your heart filled with love toward everyone, like your Christ who died for the disobedient, and be confident that He will rejoice in you and support you.

6.8.4.en: (3) Not mingling with the wicked (vv. 14-18 - ch. 7:1) 14 "Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness? 15 And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel? 16 And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. 17 Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you, 18 And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty. Ch. 7:1 Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God."

6.9.0.en: Yoke: a crossbeam placed on the necks of two animals to join them together, with a perpendicular beam attached to its middle, at the end of which is the farming implement such as the plow.

6.9.1.en: The Law of Moses decreed that a yoke should not be placed on two animals of different kinds, because the strength of one differs from the other, so they cannot pull the farming implement in a balanced way. The spiritual purpose of this law was that believers should not mingle with unbelievers.

6.9.2.en: And here St. Paul confirms this truth, warning the believers not to mingle with unbelievers and the wicked at idol-worship feasts or any celebrations not fitting for the children of God, so that they do not share with them in doing evil. He gives as the reason that there can be no mixture between sin and righteousness because they are repugnant to each other, and likewise between light and darkness because they are opposites. Likewise the conduct and life of the children of God cannot agree and share with the wicked in their wickedness.

6.10.0.en: Belial: a Hebrew name meaning "wicked," by which Satan is meant.

6.10.1.en: The Apostle affirms the necessity of believers' not mingling with unbelievers, just as there can be no agreement between the leader of each party, that is, Christ and Satan. Likewise the portion and reward of each party differ: the believers have the Kingdom of Heaven, while the unbelievers who reject Christ have eternal torment.

6.11.0.en: The Apostle argues for the necessity of believers' not mingling with pagan unbelievers by saying that believers are the temple of God, set apart for His worship, which is completely different from what is set apart for the worship of idols, that is, the wicked unbelievers, because the believer, by his prayers, worship and service, becomes a temple of God. The Apostle confirmed his words with verses from the Holy Bible, that the children of God are temples for Him in which He dwells and walks among them (1 Cor 3:16), and likewise He is their God whom they worship, and He takes them as a people of His own, as He said in (Jer 31:33).

6.12.0.en: Paul relies on the word of God in Isaiah (Isa 52:11), and calls the believers in Corinth to keep away from unbelievers and reject their evil works and not be present in their assemblies filled with sin; then God receives them as sons and rejoices in them.

6.13.0.en: Paul also borrows God's word to David in (2 Sam 7:14) to affirm God's love for the believers who separate themselves from the wicked and the unbelievers, by granting them His fatherhood and caring for them as His children.

6.13.1.en: Let your heart be open in love to everyone, but be careful to preserve your purity by keeping away from mingling with the wicked. You will meet the people of the world and deal with them well in all areas of life and love them and serve them, but take care that their strange thoughts do not enter your heart, so that you always live by the word of God and His commandments.
